complexity.notes: The conditional increment does two dict lookups per element; dict.get(num, 0) or a defaultdict would do one. The final list(set(...)) is only needed because a repeated frequency in the top-k slice causes the same keys to be collected twice — iterating over dict items and sorting by count directly would avoid both the rescans and the dedup. The O(n log n) sort is not optimal: an O(n) approach exists via ||bucket sort indexed by frequency||, which the generalized problem allows since counts lie in [1, n].
complexity.summary: Builds a frequency dict, sorts the frequency values, takes the top k, then rescans the dict once per chosen frequency to collect every key with that count, deduplicating with a set at the end.
